payload.goal: Move sofar's hot path to a native Rust core without a big-bang rewrite: lock the black-box contract (SPEC plus a conformance suite over commands, hooks and record format), build sofar-core in Rust (hook handlers, event append, fold, digest/status render, statusline) behind the same CLI contract, integrate with TypeScript fallback, ship prebuilt per-platform binaries via npm, and prove it as its own benchmark arm; it ships only if no held-out lead margin shrinks (bench-refresh D19). After conformance parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only.

payload.because:
- Sofar runs on every tool call of every agent session. A native core gives near-zero hook start-up, fast folds over very large records (this repo's own is 9.7 MB), a single binary with no Node dependency for Codex/Cursor/OpenCode users, and headroom for many parallel agents.
- Measured 0.31 hooks are only ~0.75% of session time today, so the win is future scale and distribution rather than today's tokens. That is why it goes incrementally, and must pass the same benchmark gate as any other change.
- A conformance-first strangler port means neither implementation can drift from the SPEC.
payload.chose:
Adopt Rust for sofar's HOT PATH, incrementally, starting now. Ruled by the run owner 2026-09-15 ("yes do it").
SUPERSEDES, for the hot path only, the CLAUDE.md engineering conventions:
- "TypeScript strict mode; Node ≥18; ES modules";
- "Dependencies: … Nothing else without logging a Decision". Rust crates are limited to serde, serde_json and ulid until another Decision adds one.

Scope of `sofar-core`: hook handlers (session-start, user-prompt-submit, post-tool-use, stop, session-end), atomic event append, fold, digest/status render, and statusline.

TypeScript keeps: the MCP server, `sofar drive`, init/doctor/review, and cloud commands.

The contract comes first: docs/SPEC.md plus a black-box conformance suite over commands, hook stdin/stdout, env and record bytes. It runs against BOTH implementations.

The schema rail holds: event payload types stay authored ONLY in packages/schema/src. Rust types are GENERATED from them, never hand-written. Projection templates keep one source of truth, and Rust output is verified byte-identical by golden tests.

Parity gate: 100% conformance, perf targets met, and a benchmark arm "sofar-rust-core" vs "sofar-ts" that shrinks no D19 lead margin.

Sequencing: r1-fixes waves 1–2 land in TypeScript now, and the Rust core must reach parity INCLUDING them. After parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only, which stops the TypeScript port surface growing. Distribution: prebuilt per-platform binaries through npm optionalDependencies, with a TypeScript fallback.
payload.over:
- A big-bang rewrite now: it freezes waves 1–3, leaves round 2 unable to attribute gains, and means porting 27.6k engine lines and 34k test lines before anything is trustworthy.
- Staying TypeScript-only behind a measure-first gate: the run owner's point is that the port cost grows with every feature, and Codex CLI, Turborepo and Biome show the path is proven.
payload.rule: Hot-path event and projection behaviour is defined by docs/SPEC.md plus the conformance suite and must pass against both the TypeScript and Rust implementations; Rust schema types are generated from packages/schema/src, never hand-written.

plan.goal: Move sofar's hot path to a native Rust core incrementally (rust-core D1): contract first, then sofar-core in Rust behind the same CLI and hook contract, integrated with TypeScript fallback, shipped as prebuilt binaries, and proven as its own benchmark arm that shrinks no held-out lead margin (bench-refresh D19). After parity, new hot-path code is Rust-only.

tasks.title: Inventory the hot-path surface from docs/SPEC.md and engine code: every hook's stdin/stdout/exit behaviour, CLI commands in scope (event append, status, statusline), env vars, files written, event envelope and projection outputs. List every SPEC gap found.

Black-box conformance suite in the TS repo: runs an implementation binary against golden fixtures (real records including this repo's 9.7 MB log, calib and smoke cells, corrupt and unknown lines, concurrent appends) and compares stdout, exit codes and record bytes. Green on TypeScript first.
Perf baseline harness: hook p50/p95 cold start and fold/digest latency at 10, 100 and 1,000 initiatives and 1–10 MB records, TypeScript numbers recorded as the target to beat
Cargo workspace crates/sofar-core; schema codegen from packages/schema/src (no hand-written payload types); dependency list per D1
Event envelope and atomic O_APPEND append; unknown and corrupt lines skipped with a warning, never fatal, never rewritten
Fold to initiative state with conformance parity
Digest/status render byte-identical to the projection templates (golden tests), including the 10k char cap behaviour
Hook handlers (session-start, user-prompt-submit, post-tool-use, stop, session-end) with conformance parity, including r1-fixes wave 1–2 behaviour
TS entry points and hook shims dispatch to sofar-core when present, with TypeScript fallback and an explicit override for debugging
Prebuilt binaries per platform (darwin arm64/x64, linux x64/arm64, win32 x64) via npm optionalDependencies, plus a CI build matrix
Gate green: 100% conformance on both implementations and perf targets beaten
Benchmark arm sofar-rust-core vs sofar-ts under a frozen addendum; must shrink no D19 lead margin
Release after benchmark evidence (never before, per bench-refresh D20)
Switch the rule: new hot-path features are Rust-only; decide whether to port the remaining TypeScript surfaces
